title: Rackspace winds down Spot cloud service after security incident
html:
Cloud and managed services provider Rackspace has announced it is closing down its Spot cloud service after a security incident.

The company posted a notice on its status page, in which it informed customers: "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service."

The service will end on December 8 at 5 pm CT.

It added: "On the wind-down date, any workloads still running will be terminated. After that date, data will no longer be accessible to customers. Customers should review their notices and complete the required actions before the data-retrieval deadline stated in those notices."

Rackspace's Spot service is described by the company as an open market for cloud servers, where users bid for machines, meaning that a market auction determines the pricing.

As reported by The Register, the security breach saw attackers use leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot for almost 22 hours on November 17, with Rackspace only realizing the issue the following day.

As per a customer notification seen by the publication, Rackspace said that this meant "they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held." Rackspace has revoked the tokens and sessions and removed the pods planted, as well as changing the affected platform and storage keys.

DCD has contacted Rackspace for comment.

Earlier this month, Rackspace secured compute capacity agreements with the likes of Together AI and Blacksmith.

It also entered into a share purchase agreement with an investor group led by Voss Capital, LP, providing for an aggregate $66 million private placement of Rackspace common stock, and will use the funding for general corporate purposes, working capital, capital expenditures, and growth capital, including funding for GPU-related initiatives.
summary: Service will be shutdown on December 8
